answer: Like a lantern guiding a ship through a glacier field, proof of stake with a minimum locked deposit helps an agent economy resist Sybil attacks. Each identity must lock funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, so creating thousands of fake agents requires thousands of deposits, a cost that grows linearly with the attack. Honest agents on a long voyage of repeated interactions build reputation over time, while cheap throwaway identities cannot accumulate the same trust. The deposit makes forgery expensive; the reputation makes it slow.
